groups.text: It is currently 18 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

The gap between AI performance on benchmarks and real-world utility remains a significant hurdle for the industry. To test this, Databricks hosted the inaugural Grounded Reasoning Cup, a live competition evaluating how AI agents reason over complex enterprise document collections. Eleven academic teams from the U.S. and Canada used resources from labs like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind to build their systems. These teams optimized agents on the OfficeQA benchmark before facing a new corpus of 120,000 U.S. Treasury documents. The results showed that generalization cannot be assumed, as out-of-the-box frontier agents averaged less than 30 percent accuracy. A winning team from Stanford reached 63.3 percent accuracy by using an optimization strategy that combined adaptive verification with a library of reusable skills. This disparity suggests that improvements on familiar benchmarks do not always transfer reliably to new, real-world tasks.

Ukraine's parliament returned from its summer break on August 18th amid high tension over the country's leadership. The Verkhovna Rada went into recess in mid-July shortly after President Volodymyr Zelensky announced a government reshuffle that ousted popular Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. That decision triggered mass protests across Ukraine, and demonstrators are gathering near the parliament building once again to demand Fedorov's reinstatement. While Zelensky refuses to make that move, he has not yet formally nominated permanent candidates for the defense or foreign ministries. Yevhen Khmara, a veteran of the Security Service of Ukraine, has served as acting defense minister since July. Andrii Sybiha also continues to serve as acting foreign minister in Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi's new cabinet. Because these two positions are proposed by the president rather than the prime minister, any permanent appointments must now be approved by the parliament.

US negotiator Jared Kushner reports limited success in talks with representatives from Israel and Hamas. Speaking to Fox News in Tel Aviv, the son-in-law of President Donald Trump noted that the conflicting parties are barely moving. He hopes for progress within a month through the filling of tunnels and the removal of weapons. Following a meeting with Benjamin Netanjahu, the two agreed that a US general should verify the disarmament of Hamas. Until then, Netanjahu maintains there will be no withdrawal of Israeli forces from the territory. While these diplomatic efforts struggle, the European Space Agency is using satellites to track the physical toll of climate change. Data shows Western Europe experienced its warmest June on record in 2026. These extreme temperatures and lack of rain have created optimal environments for wildfires, which the ESA notes contribute up to 35 percent of greenhouse gases through burning organic matter.

Public backlash is mounting against Meta’s smart glasses in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Germany. In Germany, the NGO HateAid has filed a lawsuit against Meta, Ray-Ban, and Oakley over privacy violations, arguing the cameras allow users to film others without consent. Some public and private venues have already banned the devices, which critics describe as spyware. This tension over personal data extends to financial security, where consumer lender Heights Finance Holdings is notifying over 1.2 million people of a data breach. Hackers accessed a third-party cloud platform in May, stealing Social Security numbers, bank details, and government IDs. Shifting from earthly privacy to deep space, a new study using images from the European Space Agency’s Hera mission suggests Mars's moon Deimos was reshaped by a single violent asteroid impact. This event likely created the thick layer of dust that gives the small moon its smooth appearance.

Developers are refining the technical plumbing of local AI tools to ensure smoother installations across different operating systems. The llama.cpp project has released build b10483, which focuses on cleaning up CMake configurations and fixing xcframework builds for Apple platforms. This update introduces a namespaced alias for vendor targets, specifically moving the real target name to vendor-hash while adding a vendor::hash alias. These changes mean that consumers like mtmd and llama-gguf-hash now link against this namespaced alias rather than relying on raw include paths. The release also adds interface targets for header-only libraries including stb, sheredom, nlohmann, and miniaudio. By consolidating these into a single subdirectory, the team has streamlined how the software handles dependencies. These adjustments ensure that synced upstream sources can compile without modification while maintaining support for various environments, from Ubuntu Linux to Apple Silicon.

In Somalia, national forces repelled an assault on Monday over control of the key city of Baidoa. The government reports that troops killed nearly 30 militants during the clash, which involved attackers using vehicles laden with explosives. These forces were loyal to Islamist insurgents and a regional leader who has been ousted from power. In a different sphere of international activity, Germany has produced a global fitness sensation called Hyrox. Developed by Christian Toetzke, Michael Trautmann, and former Olympic field hockey player Moritz Fürste, the format combines eight one-kilometer runs with eight functional strength training stations. The founders analyzed the sports landscape to find a gap in established athletics, creating a standardized competition where people can challenge themselves regardless of gender or fitness level. While Somalia faces violent instability over regional control, this German-born movement has evolved into one of the fastest-growing fitness trends in the world.

Syrian courts have sentenced Wassim al-Assad to death for war crimes and crimes against humanity. Judge Fakhr al-Din al-Aryan ruled that the cousin of ousted president Bachar al-Assad was guilty of murder and the intentional killing of several people involving torture and brutality. This follows a trial that began in April targeting officials responsible for atrocities during the civil war. Wassim is the first member of the Assad family to be judged in person, while Bachar al-Assad, who fled to Russia, was sentenced to death in absentia last week. In other news, the Amsterdam-based Magnum Ice Cream Co N.V. has filed a Form 6-K report with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The filing, submitted on August 18, serves as a required disclosure for the foreign issuer under federal securities rules.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with rain chances up to 60 percent and temperatures between 18 and 22 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the Berlin summer holidays all day, and a visit to c-base at six in the evening. Your work calendar has a RAYX meeting at three in the afternoon.
Mail worth checking: Amazon says your package is out for delivery today. Also, Renovate requires a configuration fix for the drinks-touch repository.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
